newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Anglo-Dutch venture plans big telecoms investment.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-Dutch venture plans big telecoms investment.

text.p: Dutch state-owned rail firm Nederlandse Spoorwegen (NS) and British Telecommunications Plc (BT) said on Wednesday they planned to invest one billion guilders ($590 million) over four or five years if they won a Dutch telecoms licence.

BT and NS said last week they had applied for one of two possible licences to build and operate a national fixed-line public telephone network in competition with the current monopoly Koninklijke PTT Nederland (Dutch PTT).
The two partners will have equal investment in the new venture, to be called "Telfort".
Announcing the name, new managing director Koos van der Meulen said: "We're speaking of investing around one billion guilders in the coming years."
He saw turnover in the first year at around 150 million guilders, rising by a factor of 10 to between 1.5 billion and two billion guilders after 10 years.
The current staff of around 250 people could rise to 1,000-1,500 in the coming years, said Van der Meulen, formerly managing director of BT Nederland.

BT Nederland has been represented in the Netherlands since 1989 and currently offers business communications to Dutch-based multinationals via its "Concert" joint venture with MCI, the second largest carrier in the United States.
Key customers for Concert in the Netherlands include Shell, Philips, ABN AMRO, Unilever and Reed Elsevier.

Pat Gallagher, director of BT Europe told the news conference: "We are delighted to have reached this stage in the development of our plans for the Dutch market. In NS we have found a partner which shares our vision for extending telecommunications choice in the Netherlands."
Telfort will initially offer data, corporate voice and virtual private networks, as well as international voice and data services from Concert.
The new venture will also offer management and outsourcing with a full national portfolio of products and services once a licence has been awarded.
The Dutch transport ministry, which oversees telecoms, has said it could award one or two licences and expects to announce its decision before the end of this year.
The Netherlands plans full liberalisation of its telecoms market, the fifth largest in Europe valued at around 15 billion guilders, by January 1, 1998.
Telfort said it was developing plans to serve the Dutch residential market and mobile market.
"Our mission is that we're the alternative for national and international telephony services. The alternative in the Netherlands," said Van der Meulen.

Two other groups have also applied for Dutch fixed line licences. One is Enertel, a consortium of Dutch regional power companies and local cable television network operators. The other is Global One, a joint venture of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom. ($1=1.695 Guilder)
